definition: A parameter-efficient fine-tuning method that learns small low-rank updates instead of full weight matrices.
details: LoRA freezes the original weights and adds a small trainable low-rank decomposition to each of them, cutting trainable parameters by orders of magnitude. It dramatically reduces the memory and storage needed to adapt a model and allows many lightweight task-specific adapters to be swapped onto one base model.

citation.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
